arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: The state advocate said voters followed Supreme Court guidance. They adopted a top-two system to balance interests.
The party advocate said the law converts a core right into a mere endorsement. It undermines the party's ability to win public support.
Justice Scalia noted a candidate can join a party. He said a party cannot disassociate from that candidate.
Justice Roberts asked if the described ballot format was accurate. He sought clarity on the final ballot appearance.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The state wants to keep the top-two system. It wants to force parties to share the ballot with outsiders.
The party wants to stop the forced sharing. It wants to control who appears on its ballot line.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The state argues the law follows Supreme Court guidance. It claims the system respects party autonomy while allowing outsider access.
The party argues the law strips its core rights. It claims the state turned its right to choose nominees into a mere endorsement.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Scalia asked if the ballot shows party preference for a candidate.
Justice Alito asked if the initiative aimed to change the system minimally after a prior case.
